text: {"status": "answered", "answer": "Under the Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy v1.6, a consumer loan payment is treated as late if it is not received within 15 calendar days after the due date shown on the billing statement. If the last day of the grace period falls on a weekend or Federal Reserve holiday, the grace period is extended to the next business day. When a payment is late, Harbor assesses a single late fee equal to 5% of the scheduled payment amount or $25.00, whichever is less. Only one late fee is charged per scheduled payment, and late fees are not charged on loans enrolled in an approved hardship program while the member is meeting the program terms.", "cited_chunk_ids": ["loan_late_payment_policy::layout::B_structure::0002", "loan_late_payment_policy::layout::B_structure::0003"], "reason": "The passages directly answer when a payment is considered late and specify the late fee amount and conditions."}
